title: Reject reset-aware high-water checkpoint worker
impact: Moonshot follow-up to exp 233: observed-reset/high-water re-arming removes the asynchronous worker's level-trigger storm and preserves the off-writer first-crossing win, improving threshold-crossing p50 by 53.0% / 63.9% across the order flip while foreground reads also improve. The load-bearing sustained lane still rejects the runtime: awaited 8 KiB write p50 regresses +152.5% / +138.1%, p95 +148.8% / +163.0%, and p99 +203.9% / +161.7%. PASSIVE checkpoints can return successfully with partial progress, and two candidate repeats strand 9,165 / 10,316 pending WAL frames; with no bounded retry, a burst ending after that partial attempt leaves the backlog in place. A below-threshold control keeps p50 neutral, locating the damage in concurrent checkpoint/WAL dynamics rather than the worker's fixed lifecycle overhead. Independent review also found that page-count drops cannot identify an equal/larger first commit in a new WAL generation, and the isolate has no failure channel, so startup/runtime death can hang open or close. The design still requires a second keyed writable connection, isolate, FFI and mutex state, generation/error/partial-progress policy, and coalesced close draining, with no representative incidence evidence that synchronous checkpoint wall is materially user-visible. Runtime reverted; prototype preserved at `archive/exp-250`. Reopen only with a real generation signal, worker-failure propagation, bounded backoff/retry for partial PASSIVE progress, and a representative trace, or with a materially simpler SQLite-native approach.
